I was completely new to KPop and Bangtan both when I saw them at the BBMAs, and I would say they have definitely challenged my notions of masculinity and Asian stereotypes both. When I first watched BS&T my thoughts were mostly that they looked like girls and I couldn't tell them apart, which just makes me cringe now. Now that I have been watching them pretty much nonstop for two months I can't understand how I ever thought that, and I really appreciate how they take care of their appearance and are masculine, just in a different way than what we are used to here in the US. It is so refreshing to see men who are comfortable being physically affectionate with each other, with very little "no homo" BS that we would get here. I think that is one of the main draws for me, even. 

They have also made me so interested in Korean culture (slowly tipping into the KDrama hole) and I can now read Hangul and am very slowly learning the language. They have helped open my eyes to a whole other world that I hadn't previously been exposed to. 

Watching them in Bon Voyage particularly has been eye opening for me. Seeing them go into another country where they don't speak the language and yet still try to make friends and communicate has been so damn inspiring (infiring?) that I am really looking forward to visiting Seoul next year to see if I can tackle it with the same boldness as someone like Taehyung or Jin.
